---
title: "Units, signs and datums"
---

Two solvers that disagree on a sign give results that look wrong for no
visible reason. This page states the conventions for each collection. Where a
data file departs from them, the departure is in
[the column layouts](column-layouts.qmd) and
[the corrections](../data/corrections.qmd).

## Quantities

| Symbol | Name | Unit | Positive direction | Datum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U | Vertical displacement of the solid surface | m | Upward | The undeformed surface at the initial time |
| V | Horizontal displacement | m | Southward for the colatitude component | As above |
| N | Geoid displacement | m | Upward | The geoid at the initial time |
| S | Sea-surface variation | m | Upward | The sea surface at the initial time |
| RSL | Relative sea level | m | Sea level rising with respect to the solid surface | As above |
| zeta | Solid Earth topography | m | Upward, so a negative value is ocean depth | Mean sea level |
| h_UF | Thickness of the uniform water layer | m | Positive when water is added to the ocean | Zero at the initial time |

In the Spada et al. (2011) tests the colatitude is the angle from the load
centre, `V` is positive away from the load, and the rates `U_rate`, `V_rate`
and `N_rate` are stored in m/kyr in the converted files. GS writes rates in
mm/yr and VK in m/yr, which is the same quantity in two units and not a sign
difference; both agree in sign with the displacements. Residues of the Love
numbers are in 1/kyr with the sign of the paper, h_f = h_e - sum r_j / s_j,
which VB's files reverse.

Tests 5/1, 6/1 and 7/1 hold the Heaviside Love numbers h(t), l(t) and k(t),
dimensionless, against the time in kyr since the load was applied. The value
at t = 0 is the elastic value.

In test 3/2, polar motion is m = m_x + i m_y in degrees (eq. 3 of the paper).
The x axis points to longitude 0 and the y axis to longitude 90 degrees east.
The evidence is eq. 31: for the load centroid at longitude 75 degrees east, the
phase of m in the files of GS and VB is 75 - 180 = -105 degrees. The rate of
polar motion is in degrees per Myr, the unit of table 14. The change in length
of day is in ms, and a positive value is a longer day.

In test 4/1, the rotational frequencies a_j, the residues A_j and the secular
residue A_s of the polar motion transfer function are in 1/kyr. The elastic
residue A_e is dimensionless. The real part of a_j is negative, and the mode
that carries the Chandler wobble has an imaginary part of about 5e3 per kyr.

`N` is a height, and several benchmark contributors store the gravitational
potential perturbation instead. Dividing the potential by the surface gravity
gives the height; the Martinec scripts use 9.8155 m/s², the surface value of
the M3-L70-V01 gravity profile.

## Earth structure

The earth models of GIAMIP are radial. The node tables of PREM and PREM-stable
give the radius in metres from the centre of the Earth, and the rows go from
the centre to the surface. Depth is in km below the solid surface, which is at
a radius of 6371 km, so the depth is 6371 km minus the radius. The ocean of PREM
is replaced by upper crust: the ocean is a surface load, so the earth model has
no fluid layer at the top. The viscosity structures give their layers in depth
below the same surface.

A boundary between two regions appears twice in a node table, at the same
radius. The first of the two rows holds the values below the boundary and the
second the values above. `giamip.earth` asks for the side at a boundary, and its
default is the side above. Gravity in the tables is the magnitude of the
gravitational acceleration, positive. An elastic layer has an infinite
viscosity, and the viscosity structure does not describe the core.

## Angles

Both benchmarks work in colatitude, measured from the north pole, from 0 to
180 degrees. GIAMIP works in latitude, from -90 to 90, ordered south to
north. Longitude is 0 to 360 eastward in GIAMIP; the benchmarks use the same
range.

Colatitude does not run the same way in every benchmark file. Six of the
benchmark A difference files ascend from 0 and two descend from 180. See
correction `benchmarkA-colatitude-ordering`.

## Densities

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from giamip import cases
b = cases.loads("spada2011")["constants"]
g = cases.case("giamip-exp01")["constants"]
Markdown(f"""
| Quantity | Benchmarks | GIAMIP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ice density (kg/m3) | {b['ice_density_kg_m3']} | {g['ice_density_kg_m3']} |
| Ocean water density (kg/m3) | {b['water_density_kg_m3']} | {g['ocean_water_density_kg_m3']} |
| Fresh water density (kg/m3) | {b['water_density_kg_m3']} | {g['fresh_water_density_kg_m3']} |
| Earth radius (m) | {b['earth_radius_m']:.0f} | {g['earth_radius_m']} |
""")
```

::: {.callout-important}
The densities differ between the two, which is why every case carries its own
constants and no shared constants module exists. A module would give one
collection the other's values and report nothing.
:::

## Reference frame

GIAMIP requires output in the centre of mass frame of the whole Earth system,
which includes the solid Earth and the surface mass redistribution, and not
the centre of mass of the solid Earth alone. Protocol section 6.1 asks that
the treatment of degree one and any conversion between the two frames be
documented in the model report.

Spada et al. (2011) test 7/1 requires the degree one loading Love numbers in
the centre of mass frame.

## Time

The benchmarks measure time in thousands of years from the moment of loading,
with `t = 0` the instant the load is applied.

GIAMIP measures time in years from 2000 CE, which is model year 0. Negative
is the past. The prescribed interval runs from 122 ka or 80 ka before 2000 CE
to 1000 years after it, at 500-year steps before 26 ka and 100-year steps
after. The forcing files carry both a `time` variable in days since
2000-01-01 on a 365-day calendar and a `year` variable holding the offset in
years, whose `long_name` is wrong; see correction `ice-year-longname`.

## Spherical harmonics

GIAMIP requires the optional Stokes coefficients as fully normalised real
spherical harmonics with 4 pi normalisation, dimensionless, at a reference
radius of 6371000 m, for degrees 0 to 96. A different internal convention
must be converted before submission.

## GIAMIP output of the G-ADOPT runs {#giamip-output}

This section defines the quantities in the GIAMIP files of the G-ADOPT
submission, group `G-ADOPT`, model `g-adopt`. The `references` attribute of
every file links here. The general GIAMIP conventions above, under
[Reference frame](#reference-frame), [Time](#time) and
[Spherical harmonics](#spherical-harmonics), also apply.

| Variable | Definition | Positive direction | Datum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delta_bed` | Radial displacement of the solid surface, u . r̂ | Upward | The bed at the first output |
| `delta_g` | Change of N + Shift, with N = (ψ + ψ_rot) / g_s | Sea surface rising | N + Shift at the first output |
| `delta_bed_east` | Horizontal displacement, u . ê_east | Eastward | The surface at the first output |
| `delta_bed_north` | Horizontal displacement, u . ê_north | Northward | The surface at the first output |
| `ocean_area_fraction` | Cell mean of B, 1 over open water and floating ice | | |
| `land_ice_area_fraction` | Cell mean of [I > 1 mm], grounded and floating ice | | |

N is the geoid of the solver: the gravitational potential ψ plus the
rotational potential ψ_rot, divided by the surface gravity g_s. Shift is the
uniform change of the sea surface that conserves the total mass of ice and
ocean water. So `delta_g` is the change of the sea surface equipotential and
includes its uniform part.

Each variable carries a `reference` attribute with its datum, from the
"Reference" column of the data request. For `delta_bed_east` and
`delta_bed_north` that column says "Geoid at initial simulation timestep",
which repeats the `delta_g` row. The files give "Bedrock position at initial
simulation timestep" for these two, the datum of a horizontal displacement.

The six scalar series are integrals on the native surface mesh of the
solver, computed before any regridding, as protocol section 6.1 asks. I is
the ice thickness, SL the water depth of the solver at the same step, B the
ocean without grounded ice and C the ocean including the marine regions
under grounded ice.

- `mean_delta_g` is ∫ `delta_g` B dS / ∫ B dS, the mean of `delta_g` over
  the ocean of the same step, open water and floating ice. It differs from
  the barystatic estimate from `maf`, because the mean of the sea-surface
  change over the ocean also contains the mean change of the sea floor
  under the ocean, and the ocean area B itself changes between steps as the
  coastline moves.
- `maf` is ρ_i ∫ max(0, I - (ρ_w / ρ_i) max(SL, 0)) dS, the ice mass above
  flotation, with ρ_w and ρ_i the ocean water and ice densities of the
  case file (the GIAMIP column of the [Densities](#densities) table). The
  integrand is zero
  where the ice floats or where there is no ice.
- `grd_ice_mass` is ρ_i ∫ (1 - B) I dS, `total_ice_mass` is ρ_i ∫ I dS,
  `ocean_area` is ∫ B dS and `ocean_area_grdice` is ∫ C dS.

The four displacement and geoid fields are the values of the finite-element
fields at the Gauss-Legendre nodes, with no smoothing.

::: {.callout-warning}
The method that averages the two fractions over each grid cell is not
decided yet (plan decision A4). This paragraph is a placeholder. Until the
method is decided, the `comment` attribute of each fraction names the method
of the file.
:::

The runs of Exp09, Exp10 and Exp12 write output at a subset of the forcing
years. The files carry every forcing year. At a year with no model output,
each value is the linear interpolation in time between the two neighbouring
model outputs, and at a model output year the value is the model value. The
`comment` attribute of each variable names the interpolated years. The other
experiments write output at every forcing year, and no value is
interpolated.

`Clm` and `Slm` are the coefficients of `delta_g` at the final output minus
`delta_g` at the first output, in the basis of protocol section 7:

$$
\delta g(\theta, \phi) = R \sum_{l=0}^{96} \sum_{m=0}^{l}
\left(C_{lm} \cos m\phi + S_{lm} \sin m\phi\right) \bar P_{lm}(\cos\theta),
\qquad
\bar P_{lm} = \sqrt{(2 - \delta_{m0})(2l+1)\frac{(l-m)!}{(l+m)!}}\, P_{lm},
$$

with R = 6371000 m, θ the colatitude, and P_lm the associated Legendre
function without the Condon-Shortley phase (-1)^m. The integral of the
square of each basis function over the sphere is 4π. The coefficients come
from Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the gridded `delta_g`, which is exact on
this grid to degree 96. They are stored as (degree, order) arrays of 97 × 97,
with zeros where the order is larger than the degree.

The solver constrains the centre of mass of the solid Earth and the surface
load to the origin at every step. The outputs are therefore in the CM frame
with no conversion from CE. In this frame the degree-1 part of `delta_g` is
close to zero, and the degree-1 part of the displacement is not zero,
because it is the motion of the solid Earth relative to the centre of mass
of the whole system.

Each file names the version and the commit of the giamip code that wrote it
in its `references` attribute. The global attributes with the prefix `run_`
copy the attributes of the intermediate file of the export, for example the
G-ADOPT commit, the Firedrake and PETSc versions, the mesh, k_s and C - A.
